meta.title: TugQL — a portable, human-readable query language
meta.description: TugQL is a portable, human-readable query language. One query runs unchanged across Git, SQLite, PostgreSQL and Firestore — featuring an intuitive SQL-like text syntax and a lossless, schema-validated query tree (TugQT).
meta.ogDescription: TugQL: portable, human-readable query language and structured query tree (TugQT) across backends.
meta.jsonLdDescription: A portable, human-readable query language and structured query tree (TugQT) for databases and data abstraction layers.

hero.lede: TugQL is a portable, human-readable query language. It combines a clean SQL-like text syntax with a 1:1, lossless structured query tree representation (TugQT) serialized as plain YAML/JSON. Save a query, hand-edit it, diff it in version control, and execute it across backends without loss.

why.title: A query is data. Treat it like data.
why.kicker: TugQL turns a query into an understandable, diffable document you can store, review, and version — portable across every backend it runs on.

cards.title: Human-readable
cards.body: Intuitive SQL-like authoring syntax for people, plus plain YAML/JSON query tree (TugQT) for tooling — anyone can inspect it, understand it, and edit it.

cards.title: Lossless round-trip
cards.body: Canonical query lowering reconstructs queries structurally equal to the source. Nothing is silently dropped, mangled, or approximated.

cards.title: Schema-validated
cards.body: Published with full JSON Schema validation (draft 2020-12). Any tool, in any language, can validate a query structure before execution.

cards.title: Diff-friendly
cards.body: Canonical formatting and deterministic tree serialization. Saved queries diff cleanly in Git and review like standard code.

cards.title: Portable by design
cards.body: TugQL exposes functionality that is portable across backends, so one query runs unchanged across Git, SQLite, PostgreSQL, or Firestore.

cards.title: Not full SQL
cards.body: A deliberately focused, well-defined portable subset. Unportable constructs are rejected explicitly rather than translated dangerously.

example.title: A query as TugQL & TugQT
example.kicker: Author in TugQL text syntax; persist or exchange as a TugQT structured query tree.
example.p1: Authors write queries in TugQL text syntax — readable, compact, and SQL-like. Underneath, the parser produces TugQT (Tug Query Tree), a canonical, machine-readable representation.
example.p2: Every node maps deterministically between syntax and tree. Malformed input or schema violations return actionable diagnostics with precise source spans. Text queries take -- and // end-of-line comments; the YAML form uses #.
example.noteText: TugQL was previously published at dtql.org, which now redirects permanently to tugql.org.

mapping.title: Mapping
mapping.kicker: Each in-scope query node has a defined structured representation.

rows.rep: item under columns: — an expression plus optional as:
item under orderBy: — an expression plus optional desc: true

mapping.caption: An expression sets exactly one of field, value or values, which discriminates a field reference, a constant, or an array.

scope.title: What TugQL represents
scope.kicker: Single source collections or joined trees, selected columns, filter expressions, ordering, and paging. Anything out of scope is rejected — never silently dropped.
scope.inScopeBody: Collection sources · selected columns · comparison and And/Or group trees · ordering · limit / offset · joins · parameters. Expressions: field reference, constant, array. Operators: ==, !=, In, >, >=, <, <=, And, Or.
scope.outScopeBody: Unbounded cartesian joins · arbitrary dialect-specific vendor syntax · untyped mutation operators outside schema authority. Serialization errors out — it never emits a document that loses query semantics.
scope.losslessBody: resolve(parse(text)) produces deterministic query trees; serialization is canonical, so saved queries diff cleanly across versions.

stack.title: One query, many backends
stack.kicker: TugQL is the portable query surface. It maps onto a data abstraction layer (DALgo) that adapts it to whatever storage sits underneath.
stack.p: Because TugQL expresses the portable subset, a query written once behaves consistently whether resolving against a Git repository (inGitDB), an embedded SQLite file, a PostgreSQL database, or Firestore.
stack.flowAria: TugQL maps through a data abstraction layer to several storage backends

implementations.title: Specification & implementations
implementations.kicker: The language is an open specification with a published schema and implementations in Go and TypeScript.

cards.title: tugql/tugql
cards.desc: The TugQL specification, the canonical JSON Schema (draft 2020-12), and validated example documents.

cards.title: dal-go/dalgo/tugql
cards.desc: The Go library: parse, validate, resolve, format, and execute TugQL queries with lossless round-trip guarantees.

datatug.title: Explore data and query it with DataTug.
datatug.kicker: DataTug helps developers explore database schemas, build and run queries, and understand results. Its work on query contracts with TugQL and TugQT is ongoing. Explore the tools behind DataTug.

closing.title: Save it. Diff it. Run it anywhere.
closing.p: TugQL makes a query a first-class, reviewable artifact — readable by people, validated by tooling, and portable across the backends it runs on.

footer.tag: An open, portable query language. Canonical home: tugql.org
